newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Lack of rain threatens Angolan harvests - WFP.
newsitem.headline: Lack of rain threatens Angolan harvests - WFP.

text.p: Inadequate rain in several of Angola's western provinces poses a serious threat to this year's harvest of corn and other crops and could result in a food shortage, according to officials in Luanda.
"We are taking this very seriously," said Sonsoles Ruedas, the World Food Programme (WFP) officer for the northern region of Angola.
"It hasn't rained in many of the provinces and we know that seeds distributed and planted in December have not grown."
Food security experts in Luanda say areas of Bengo, Cuanza Sul, Cuanza Norte, Luanda, Malange and Zaire Provinces have been the most affected by the lack of rain.

Ruedes said she had received unconfirmed reports of increased rates of malnutrition in Zaire province. WFP field workers were reporting that many rural families had only enough stores of manioc (a staple in Angola) to last until April.
But Ruedes said it was impossible to know how serious the situation was until a proper assessment of crops in the provinces had been finished.
"Something is happening, but how serious it is we just don't know yet," said Ruedes. "We will be sending an assessment team out as early as next week."
